svg.title: CI/CD pipeline security and workload identity architecture
svg.desc: Three panels. The first lists representative OWASP CI/CD risks: CICD-SEC-4 Poisoned Pipeline Execution with its three vectors D-PPE, I-PPE and 3PE; CICD-SEC-6 insufficient credential hygiene from static cloud keys held in secret stores; and CICD-SEC-3 dependency chain abuse. The second describes the OIDC workload identity exchange: the runner requests a short-lived JWT from its CI platform, exchanges it through AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity or the equivalent, has the trust policy pin both the audience and the subject claim rather than the repository alone, and receives temporary credentials lasting one hour by default. The third covers pipeline hardening: branch protection, ephemeral isolated runners, and scoping secrets to protected branches and approval-gated environments. A bottom bar summarizes the flow from code review through runner allocation and token exchange to deployment.
svg.text: CI/CD Pipeline Security & Workload Identity
OWASP CI/CD Top 10 risks, Poisoned Pipeline Execution (PPE), and passwordless OIDC workload identity federation.
OWASP CI/CD SECURITY RISKS
Pipeline Attack Vectors & Compromise
• CICD-SEC-4: Poisoned Pipeline Execution — three vectors,
D-PPE, I-PPE and 3PE, each from a different access level
• CICD-SEC-6: Insufficient Credential Hygiene (static cloud
keys held in pipeline secret stores)
• CICD-SEC-3: Dependency Chain Abuse
OIDC WORKLOAD IDENTITY FEDERATION
Passwordless Short-Lived Cloud Tokens
• 1. Runner requests a short-lived OIDC JWT from its platform
• 2. Exchange via AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity (AWS STS / GCP)
• 3. Trust policy pins aud and sub — not repository alone
• 4. Temporary credentials, one hour by default
PIPELINE HARDENING & GOVERNANCE CONTROLS
Least-Privilege Execution & Branch Protection
• Branch protection and mandatory review: contains D-PPE and I-PPE, where the attacker already holds repository write access
• Fork pull-request approval gate: contains 3PE, where the attacker holds no access at all — the other two controls do not reach it
• Ephemeral isolated runners, third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs, and secrets scoped to protected branches
CI/CD SECURITY FLOW: PR CODE REVIEW → EPHEMERAL RUNNER ALLOCATION → OIDC TOKEN EXCHANGE → SECURE DEPLOYMENT
